messages:
rob: deploy-bot flagged dedicated eu-west-1 pool: p95 latency +60% and sim-drop ~4% on model redwood-3.0.0-canary
deploy-bot: auto-check at 2024-09-10T08:12Z — trigger: p95>250ms && sim_delta<=-3%. Suggested: PAUSE rollout or target rollback to 3.0.0-stable
maya: is this only dedicated? any hosted customers affected?
phil: dedicated eu-west-1 only (8% traffic). hosted showed no change. infra note: quant kernel fallback occurred for AVX fallback path.
oncall: tagging @maya @sara — recommend targeted soft-rollback for dedicated pool, monitor for 20m, then decide. Avoid global revert unless errors.
sara: agree. run targeted rollback command:
```
redwoodctl pool rollback --pool=dedicated-euw1 --to-version=3.0.0-stable --reason "p95 + sim regression"
```
rob: rolling now. notifying on-call and customer success if we widen.
deploy-bot: rollback initiated by rob at 2024-09-10T08:18Z. status: draining connections.
phil: p95 dropped back to baseline in 5m, sim delta now -0.2%. KV-hit recovered.
maya: keep dedicated pinned to 3.0.0-stable for 60m. start eval-runner 500 samples across long-context prompts.
rob: disabling autopromote for change window: `deploy-bot config set autopromote.enabled false --until 2024-09-10T10:30Z`
sara: customer blurb draft (only if we widen): "We observed increased latency for some workloads in eu-west dedicated pool during the 3.0.0 rollout. We've rolled that pool back to 3.0.0-stable and are investigating. No errors reported. Update in 60m."
rob: summary added to release-notes/internal: "Dedicated euw1 rolled back to 3.0.0-stable after canary-like regression; autopromote paused; investigating kernel selection." :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: thread auto-archived at 2024-09-10T09:00Z (manual hold still active).
